[center][b]GODLY HAND Scene Builder — Sneak Peek Release [BETA][/b][/center]
[center]"Tested extensively in development but real-world NPC projects will surface edge cases I couldn't reproduce alone. If something breaks, drop it in the comments with your setup and I'll fix it."

[left]📌 Main Purpose This is a sneak peek at two more components of Godly Hand — a full all-in-one NPC creator coming to Nexus. This release includes the Event Builder and the Coordinate Picker — the tools that replace the most painful parts of writing a custom Stardew Valley event.[/left]
[/center]
If you have ever written a custom event, you know the loop. You open a text editor and start writing a slash-delimited string from memory. You look up the internal map name because ScienceHouse is not something you could guess. You type an event ID that feels unique and find out later — in-game, with no useful SMAPI error — that it was already a vanilla ID all along. You need a tile coordinate, so you boot the game, find the tile, write the number on a sticky note, quit, and go back to the string. You forget that the move command takes a delta, not a destination, so your NPC slides off the edge of the map. You add a player choice and it works perfectly except the question just keeps asking itself in a loop with no error, no log, nothing — because one of your answer labels had a portrait token in it. You didn't know that broke it. Nobody told you. The game didn't tell you. You found a four-year-old forum post that told you.
Set your conditions from dropdowns. Click a tile on a rendered map to save its coordinates. Build your scene command by command with a helper that shows you exactly what each command does. Run a syntax check that finds the $ token loop before you ever touch the game. Download a Content Patcher-ready JSON. That is the Event Builder.
Use it alongside the Coordinate Picker — load any map file, click tiles, label them, organise them into folders, and pull them directly into the Event Builder when you need a position.
Interested in the other tools? Check out the rest of the Godly Hand rollout: Animation Builder: https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/[ID] Coordinate Picker: https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/47616 Debug Commands: https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/47582

🎬 Event Builder Features
🆔 Event ID generation with a full vanilla collision check There are hundreds of vanilla Stardew event IDs spread across the base game, and they aren't sequential. Any one of them can silently steal your event if you accidentally use the same number. Click Generate and the tool checks every vanilla ID, every ID already in your current session, and the last ID it generated, then picks the next free number in the custom NPC band — 9871000 and up, past where the base game ends. Type your own ID instead and the syntax checker catches a vanilla collision before it becomes your problem.
🗺️ Map picker that tells you what the maps actually are The internal names are not obvious. ScienceHouse is Robin and Demetrius's home. JoshHouse is George and Evelyn's. The map dropdown lists every Stardew location with its internal name and a plain-English description of what it actually is and who lives there. Select one and the right name goes into the event key automatically. For maps not in the list — modded locations, custom maps — there is a custom entry field.
⚙️ Trigger conditions built from fields, not memorised flag syntax Hearts required, prerequisite event IDs, days of the week, time windows, weather conditions, dating and marriage flags, and extra friendship checks for multiple NPCs — all set via form fields, assembled into the correct slash-delimited key automatically. The heart field takes hearts, not friendship points — 8 hearts becomes 2000 in the output without you touching a calculator. Prerequisite event IDs can be typed by hand or picked from a dropdown of IDs already in your loaded file or current session.
🎵 Music by the name you know it by The music field is a categorised dropdown — Seasonal, Festival, Character, Location, Mood, and more — with every vanilla track listed by the name you'd actually recognise. "Tropicala" not "summer2." "Stardrop Saloon" not "Saloon1." Custom or unlisted cues can always be typed in, and a loaded event that uses an unusual cue will never have it replaced or lost.
📍 NPC and farmer start positions pulled from saved coordinates Place each actor's starting tile and facing direction at the top of the scene. Any field that takes a tile position shows a 📍 Saved button when you have coordinates saved in the Coordinate Picker — click it and a dropdown of your saved tiles appears, organised by folder. Pick a tile and the X, Y, and direction all fill in at once. If a named NPC has no start position set, the position warning panel flags it before you can generate.
✍️ Safe Edit and Direct Syntax — two ways to work the same scene The scene command panel has a mode toggle. Direct Syntax is the raw text area — every command on its own line, edit anything by hand. Safe Edit renders the same text as a clickable list. Blue lines are commands the builder knows how to edit — click one and it reopens in its builder pre-filled with its current values, ready to change. Reorder any line with the ▲ ▼ arrows. Copy a line with ⧉ and paste it anywhere in the sequence with the dashed paste zones that appear between lines. Delete a line with ×. Direct Syntax and Safe Edit are the same text — switching between them never loses anything.
🧰 Command palette with a builder for every major command A row of colour-coded buttons covers every common event command across six groups: Movement in blue, Timing in yellow, Dialogue in purple, Animation in green, Audio in violet, Camera in teal. Hover any button for its exact syntax snippet and a plain-language description of what it does and when. Click it to open a dedicated form for that command — fill in the fields, and the finished line is inserted exactly where your cursor is in the scene. Commands already in the scene can be clicked in Safe Edit to reopen the same form pre-filled, change what you need, and overwrite the line.
➡️ Move builder with tile math The move command takes a delta, not a destination. That is the thing people get wrong. The move builder has two modes. Type Numbers lets you enter dx and dy directly. Tile Math reads your saved coordinates, shows you a start tile and an end tile dropdown, picks the right axis, and computes the offset for you — it even warns you when the two tiles differ on both axes and you need a second move command for the diagonal. Facing direction is a required dropdown, not an optional afterthought, so you can't accidentally ship an event where your NPC just slides past and keeps looking south.
🎞️ Visual frame picker for the animate command The animate command takes a space-separated list of frame numbers. Writing that list by hand and getting it right on the first try is not something that happens. Click the frame picker button inside the animate builder, load the actor's spritesheet PNG, and every frame is laid out in a grid — your actual pixels. Click frames in the order you want them to play. A live preview to the right plays your sequence at the exact milliseconds-per-frame the animate command uses — what you see is what the game runs. Frames already in the sequence show their position number below them. Click the same frame multiple times for a back-and-forth. Click Undo to remove the last pick.
💬 Dialogue tag helper with hover descriptions Every speak, message, and textAboveHead field has a tag panel below it. Portrait expressions ($0 through $5), dynamic text inserts (@, %spouse, %farm, %pet, %name), and structural tags like #$b# for a new dialogue box are all listed as clickable buttons. Click any tag to insert it at your cursor position. Hover it for a description of exactly what it does and where it's valid. Advanced tags — $c for chance-based dialogue, $d for world state checks, $y for quick yes/no responses — are behind a toggle so they don't clutter the panel until you need them.
❓ Player choice and branching You can add a choice question to any event. Give the question a speaker, write the question text, and add as many answer options as you need — each with its own label, dialogue key, and branch script. Every branch gets its own scene panel where you write what happens after the player picks that option: moves, emotes, friendship changes, more dialogue, a day-end if you want one. The branch is a full subscene, not a single line. Multiple independent question sequences in the same event are also supported — add an extra fork group, place it in the scene with a marker button that drops exactly at your cursor, and each group handles its own question and answers independently.
🔌 ValleyTalk-aware fork generation The fork system knows about ValleyTalk. Toggle it per fork group and the builder automatically registers each answer's response key as a dialogue entry in the correct character's Dialogue file alongside the event — the Characters/Dialogue block the tool generates handles all of it. If you loaded a file that uses ValleyTalk and then change your mind, one button strips every ValleyTalk-specific block from the session output, clears the VT response keys from the Characters/Dialogue entries, and removes any dialogue blocks that end up empty. Everything else stays untouched.
[url=https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/30319]https://www.nexusmods.com/stardewvalley/mods/30319[/url] 
🔍 Syntax check that catches the silent ones Run a full check any time before generating. It catches the things SMAPI doesn't flag clearly: event IDs that collide with vanilla, time windows where start is not less than end, time values past the 2400 hard cap, conflicting Dating and Marriage conditions, and actors with no start position. It also catches the $ token loop — the bug where a portrait tag ($0, $h, and so on) ends up inside a choice label rather than the question or the branch dialogue, which makes the choice silently re-ask itself in-game forever with no error in the log. When that's found, a Strip button appears that removes the offending tokens from every answer label in the scene and all fork panels in one click, without touching question text or branch dialogue where portrait tokens are valid.
📂 Load an existing events file to edit Already have a Data/Events JSON? Load it and the tool parses every event entry, shows the full list with map name, event ID, trigger conditions, and any load warnings, and lets you click any entry to populate the builder — conditions, positions, music, scene commands, and branches all load from the file. Unsupported or unusual event key flags (like /c, /n, or /j) are flagged as warnings rather than silently dropped so you know what didn't transfer. Broken JSON and valid-but-wrong-format files get separate, specific error messages. The event ID from a loaded entry can be picked from the prerequisite dropdown on any other event in the same session, so your chain of events knows about its own prerequisites.
📋 Session accumulation — build a whole file without merging JSON Generate an event and it goes into the session. Build the next event, generate again, and it's added — not a separate file, the same one. The session panel shows a count of how many events are in it and tells you which one just changed. Events stack by target, so a Town event and a Beach event go into separate Data/Events blocks in the same output automatically. When you're done, download the whole thing. Clear Session to start fresh. You don't touch the JSON by hand.
🔀 Merge into an existing file Already have a file you want to add events to? Upload it alongside your session output and merge. The tool folds your new events into the existing Changes array, combining entries into matching blocks rather than duplicating them. Download the merged file ready to use.
⬇ Download or copy the output Generate once and get both options. Download saves the JSON directly to your computer, ready to drop into your mod's assets folder. Copy puts it on your clipboard. Every time you regenerate, the previous output is kept as a backup accessible with one click — so regenerating doesn't cost you anything.

📍 Coordinate Picker Features
🗺️ Load and render any Stardew map file Upload a .tbin or .tmx file and the map renders on a clickable canvas — your actual tiles, not a colour grid. Tilesheet PNGs can be loaded alongside the map file for a fully rendered view. Zoom controls let you get precise on small tiles. The coordinates of whatever tile your cursor is over show at the bottom of the canvas as you move, so you always know exactly where you are before you click.
🖱️ Click to save, label, folder, and direct When you click a tile, a save panel opens showing the map name and the X and Y you landed on. Give it a label, set the facing direction, pick a folder, and save. Every saved coordinate is immediately available in the Event Builder — any position field with an X and Y shows a 📍 Saved dropdown. Pick a saved tile and the map name, X, Y, and direction all fill in at once.
📁 Folder system for keeping positions organised Coordinates go into named folders you create. Make one folder per NPC, one per map, or whatever structure matches your project. Saved tiles display their map name, X, Y, and direction inline in the list so everything stays readable at a glance without opening anything. Rename and rearrange folders as you work.
⬇ Export and reimport across sessions Export all your folders to a plain-text .txt file that reads like a clean reference sheet — folder names, labels, map names, coordinates, directions. Import any previous export back into the tool and it merges cleanly: coordinates go into matching folder names, new folder names are added, nothing is replaced. Save the export with your mod files and you never have to remap positions from scratch.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 📥 Installation This tool runs entirely in your browser. There is nothing to install.
HTML version — recommended for most users Download GodlyHand_SceneBuilder.html Open it in Chrome, Firefox, or Edge Done — no setup required
JSX version — for Claude / React environments Download GodlyHand_SceneBuilder.jsx Drop it into Claude.ai or any React sandbox and run it
Both versions are identical in functionality. No internet connection required after downloading.
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━ 📋 Requirements
Your map file .tbin and .tmx are both supported for the Coordinate Picker. Extract base game maps from the Content folder using xnbextract or a Content Patcher bundle. Modded maps work the same way.
Tile positions must come from in-game All X/Y positions and facing directions have to come from actual play or a coordinate finder mod — Debug Mode and Tile Info on Nexus are both reliable. The Coordinate Picker can get you most of the way there if you load the map file. The tool structures your data. It does not invent positions.
A modern browser Chrome, Firefox, or Edge. No internet connection required after downloading.
